headline: Credit gave its first inch in weeks and the generals took a mile back: NVDA -5.5% into the 5th percentile of its year, 2s10s crushed to 25bp, dollar back to 102.
summary: The four-day squeeze died where it started. S&P -0.4% to 7,520.9, Nasdaq 100 -0.6%, and NVDA -5.5% to 168.89 — now -26.3% on the month, sitting in the 5th percentile of its 52-week range and 17.3% below its 200-day with relative strength -23.5%. Yesterday's 7.5% SOXX moonshot gave most of itself back (SMH -0.8%, SOXX -0.1%) with only AVGO +3.9% and TSM +2.0% holding; MU -1.1% and -29.5% on the month. SMH is -19.8% on the month at z=-2.35, QQQ/SPY z=-2.68 at the 16th percentile. Risk regime slipped again to -12 from -11. A squeeze the generals won't join twice isn't a bottom.

The genuinely new thing is credit. Spreads tightened across the entire stack for the first time in weeks: HY -8bp to 3.34, IG -2bp to 0.91, BBB -3bp to 1.13, CCC -6bp to 13.11, with HYG/IEF +0.4% and turning up. VIX -2.3% to 19.46, VIX3M -1.0%, term structure back out to 0.943, and the credit & vol composite improved to -43 from -48. Don't over-pay for one day: IG still carries z=1.19 with acceleration +0.55, BBB z=1.34 with acceleration +0.61, and on the month HY is +23bp, CCC +58bp (+426bp YTD) at the 91st percentile. HYG itself fell 0.4% on a day spreads tightened. The invoice got smaller, not cancelled.

The bill simply moved to rates and the dollar. The whole curve backed up — 3m +5bp to 4.24, 2y +5bp to 4.56, 5y +3bp, 10y +2bp to 4.88, 10y real +3bp to 2.66 (19% above its 200-day, 76th percentile) — and 2s10s flattened 7bp to 25bp, the 9th percentile of the year. That is bear flattening: the wrong kind. MOVE jumped 7.5% to 92.4 while equity vol fell, so bonds are now pricing the risk stocks stopped pricing. TLT -1.3%, IEF -0.9%, LQD -0.8%. DXY +0.6% to 102.22 at the 94th percentile, USD/CHF +0.7%, USD/CAD +0.5%, and USD/BRL +1.4% to 5.5803 at z=3.23 with acceleration +2.44 — Brazil is now a genuine spiral (EWZ -26.2% on the month, Bovespa acceleration -3.95). Core CPI is turning up at z=0.93 and the inflation composite sits at +26 even with 10y breakevens at the 6th percentile. Mortgages at 7.18% took the month's hottest trade apart in a session: ITB -3.3%, XHB -2.6%, DHI -3.8% after ITB had run +13.5%.

Underneath, the rotation is unchanged and crowded: RSP/SPY z=3.75 with acceleration +3.39, equal-weight S&P at the 94th percentile, XLV +10.6% on the month (z=2.47), XLP +9.1%, XLF +6.5%, KIE at the 97th percentile, SPLV z=2.33, versus MTUM z=-3.03, high-beta/low-vol -19.9% on the month at z=-3.09, growth/value at the 4th percentile. Single names tell it cleanly: LLY +21.5%, HD +20.7%, MCD +20.0%, UPS +17.4% against CAT -26.8% (z=-3.04), MU -29.5%, GEV -20.6%, GOOGL -18.3%, ETN -17.6%. Two things cracked today that had been working: precious metals (GDX -5.4%, GDXJ -6.0%, NEM -4.2%, gold -1.8% to 4,041, silver -2.0%) and crypto's third straight down day (ETH -3.8% to 2,050, SOL -3.8%, BTC -2.0% to 73,706, COIN at the 0th percentile of its year). The macro backdrop stays benign — claims 189k at the 0th percentile, unemployment 4.1%, JOLTS +4.6% — which is exactly why this is a positioning and discount-rate problem, not a recession.

good.text: Credit finally tightened across the whole stack: HY -8bp to 3.34, IG -2bp to 0.91, BBB -3bp to 1.13, CCC -6bp to 13.11, with HYG/IEF +0.4% and turning up after a month at z=-1.39. First broad day of spread compression in weeks.

The vol bid faded: VIX -2.3% to 19.46, VIX3M -1.0% to 20.64, term structure back out to 0.943, and the credit & vol composite improved to -43 from -48. Hedges are still cheap but the panic premium is leaking out.

Labor refuses to break: initial claims 189k at the 0th percentile of the year (-14.5% y/y), unemployment 4.1% and falling, JOLTS +4.6% to 7,523k, payrolls still rising. Growth pulse composite +7 — this is a multiple problem, not an earnings cliff.

The defensive-value rotation keeps compounding: RSP/SPY z=3.75 with acceleration +3.39, equal-weight S&P at the 94th percentile, XLV +10.6% on the month (z=2.47, rs +14.8%), XLP +9.1%, KIE at the 97th percentile with z=1.95.

Ex-US kept paying: Euro Stoxx +1.9%, DAX +1.7% (93rd percentile), CAC +1.2%, ASX +1.0%, India compounding (INDA +12.4% on the month, acceleration +2.86, USD/INR -3.0% at z=-2.91), Mexico's IPC at the 100th percentile.

Inflation expectations stay anchored despite the core CPI uptick: 5y breakeven 2.25 (16th percentile), 10y 2.20 (6th percentile), gasoline -20.3% on the month at z=-1.88. Cheap energy is still disinflating the pipeline.

bad.text: The generals broke again: NVDA -5.5% to 168.89, -26.3% on the month, 5th percentile of its 52-week range, 17.3% below its 200-day, relative strength -23.5%. SMH -19.8% and SOXX -21.4% on the month at z=-2.35; MU -29.5%. Yesterday's semi squeeze was short covering and it's already gone.

Bear flattening is the worst flattening: 3m +5bp to 4.24, 2y +5bp to 4.56, 10y real +3bp to 2.66 (19% above its 200-day), 2s10s down 7bp to 25bp — the 9th percentile of the year. MOVE +7.5% to 92.4 while VIX fell; the bond market repriced risk the equity market ignored.

Dollar back on the bid — DXY +0.6% to 102.22 at the 94th percentile, USD/CHF +0.7%, USD/CAD +0.5% — and Brazil is now a spiral: USD/BRL +1.4% to 5.5803 at z=3.23 with acceleration +2.44, EWZ -26.2% on the month, Argentina -16.8%.

Crypto's third straight down day accelerated: ETH -3.8% to 2,050 (-19.1% on the month), SOL -3.8% (-25.1%), BTC -2.0% to 73,706, MSTR -3.6% (-21.6%), COIN -2.9% at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. Ether/bitcoin at the 20th percentile.

The week's best trade unwound in a session: GDX -5.4%, GDXJ -6.0%, NEM -4.2%, gold -1.8% to 4,041 (10% below its 200-day, 10th percentile), silver -2.0%, platinum -1.1%. Gold/silver still at 78.4 with z=1.89 — the stress hedge is unwinding, not confirming.

Factor and cyclical damage is accelerating, not healing: MTUM z=-3.03, high-beta/low-vol -19.9% on the month at z=-3.09, growth/value at the 4th percentile, CAT -2.4% and -26.8% on the month at z=-3.04, GEV -3.9%, ETN -1.4%. Mortgages at 7.18% knocked ITB -3.3% and DHI -3.8%.

trades.name: Short semis against health care
trades.line: Short SMH vs long XLV: generals break, defensives compound
trades.expr: Short SMH, long XLV, dollar-neutral. Express the short leg with Dec SMH puts if you want convexity into the next AI capex headline.
trades.thesis: The semi complex is making lower highs on squeezes the leader won't join. NVDA at the 5th percentile of its year with rs -23.5% while XLV is at the 98th percentile and +14.8% relative on the month. This is a leadership handoff, not a dip.
trades.trigger: SMH -19.8% on the month at z=-2.35, SOXX -21.4%, QQQ/SPY z=-2.68; XLV +10.6% on the month at z=2.47 with acceleration +1.34 and LLY +21.5%.
trades.stop: SMH reclaiming its 200-day (currently -7.4% below) with NVDA back above the 25th percentile of its range, or XLV relative strength rolling under +5%.
trades.target: Another 10% of relative move; SMH/SPY toward the 2025 lows of the ratio.

trades.name: Short the long bond into bear flattening
trades.expr: Short TLT outright, or buy Jan 78 puts. Equivalent in futures: short ultra bond.
trades.thesis: The front end is backing up on sticky inflation while the long end refuses to rally, so duration gets no carry and no capital gain. Core CPI is turning up (z=0.93) and the inflation composite is +26 with the rates composite at -33.
trades.trigger: 3m +5bp to 4.24 and 2y +5bp to 4.56 flattened 2s10s 7bp to 25bp, the 9th percentile of the year; MOVE +7.5% to 92.4 while VIX fell 2.3%; TLT -1.3% with 30y at 5.26.
trades.stop: 10y back under 4.70 with 2s10s re-steepening above 40bp, or claims breaking above 210k.

trades.name: Own the average stock, rent the index
trades.line: Long SPW vs short QQQ on breadth at z=3.75
trades.expr: Long RSP/SPW, short QQQ, equal dollars. Fund with a QQQ call-overwrite if you need the carry.
trades.thesis: The market is up on the year with the cap-weighted leadership underwater: breadth is the trade, not the index. Equal-weight is at the 94th percentile of its range while the Nasdaq sits 0.8% below its 200-day.
trades.trigger: RSP/SPY +7.6% on the month at z=3.75 with acceleration +3.39; QQQ/SPY z=-2.68 at the 16th percentile; XLF +6.5%, XLB +6.9%, XLRE +7.1%, XRT +9.9% on the month versus XLK -15.0%.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY giving back 3% from here, or QQQ/SPY reclaiming its 200-day — mean reversion in a z=3.75 ratio is the real risk.

trades.name: India over Korea in EM
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EWY: compounding vs capitulation
trades.thesis: EM is splitting on the semiconductor cycle and the currency. India has a falling dollar cross and accelerating equity trend; Korea is a leveraged bet on the exact complex now unwinding.
trades.trigger: INDA +12.4% on the month with acceleration +2.86 and USD/INR -3.0% at z=-2.91; EWY -21.5% on the month, KOSPI -24.3% and 23.7% below its 200-day, EWY -2.1% today even after Taiwan's +4.9% bounce.
trades.stop: KOSPI reclaiming its 200-day or SOXX turning up with NVDA above 190; INDA acceleration rolling negative.

trades.name: Brazil: the currency is leading the equity down
trades.line: Short EWZ with long USD/BRL as the accelerant
trades.expr: Short EWZ; add a long USD/BRL position at half weight as the cleaner, higher-signal leg.
trades.thesis: A z=3.23 currency move with +2.44 acceleration on a day the dollar index only gained 0.6% is local, not global. Local-rate stress gets paid in equities next, and Bovespa's acceleration is already -3.95.
trades.trigger: USD/BRL +1.4% to 5.5803, +11.2% on the month, 99th percentile; EWZ -26.2% on the month at z=-3.43 with acceleration -3.46; EWZ -1.4% today versus Mexico's IPC at the 100th percentile.
trades.stop: USD/BRL back under 5.40 or EWZ reclaiming its 200-day (12.9% above here).

trades.name: Long bitcoin, short ether
trades.line: Long BTC vs short ETH: altcoin beta is the liquidation
trades.expr: Long BTC (or IBIT) against short ETH, 1:1 dollars.
trades.thesis: When crypto deleverages, the high-beta tail goes first and keeps going. Bitcoin is already turning up from a 32nd-percentile base while ether and solana are still rolling over.
trades.trigger: Third straight down day and accelerating: ETH -3.8% (-19.1% on the month) and SOL -3.8% (-25.1%) versus BTC -2.0% (-11.9%); ETH/BTC at the 20th percentile and -8.2% on the month; BTC trend turning up while ETH is rolling over.
trades.stop: ETH/BTC back above 0.0300, or BTC losing 68,000 (which would make this a beta short, not a pair).
trades.target: ETH/BTC toward 0.0255, roughly 9% on the pair.

trades.name: Energy equities still haven't marked crude
trades.line: Short XOP vs long XOM: E&P beta into a -11% week
trades.expr: Short XOP, long XOM at half-to-full weight — short the leveraged barrel, own the integrated cash flow.
trades.thesis: Brent fell 11.3% in a week and 12.2% in a month and the E&P complex has priced less than three-quarters of it. The torque works both ways and XOP carries it; XOM has the balance sheet and a rising relative-strength trend.
trades.trigger: Brent 91.92 (-11.3% w/w, -12.2% m/m, z=-1.32), RBOB -20.3% on the month at z=-1.88, DBC -5.2% on the week — yet XOP is only -8.4% on the month and rose 0.8% today, with XLE still 6.1% above its 200-day.
trades.stop: Brent reclaiming 97, or OPEC supply headlines that take WTI back above 92.
